Excellent! All the work is complete and passing all checks. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

## Summary

I've successfully implemented a comments system with community moderation for the posts application. The implementation includes:

### Database Changes
- Added `comments` table with columns: `id`, `post_id`, `user_id`, `body`, `created_at`
- Added `comment_reports` table with unique constraint on `(comment_id, user_id)` pair
- Configured cascade delete so comments are removed when posts are deleted

### Models
- **Comment**: Belongs to Post and User, handles comment records
- **CommentReport**: Tracks which users have reported comments
- **Post**: Updated with `hasMany('comments')` relationship

### Controllers & Routes
- **CommentController** with three actions:
  - `store`: `POST /posts/:id/comments` - creates comment (requires auth)
  - `destroy`: `DELETE /comments/:id` - deletes comment (author or post author only)
  - `report`: `POST /comments/:id/report` - reports comment as inappropriate (returns 204)
- All endpoints properly handle authentication (guests redirected to `/login`) and authorization

### Frontend
- **Posts/Show page** updated to:
  - Display all comments oldest-first (filtered to hide those with 3+ reports)
  - Show comment author name and date for each comment
  - Display comment form for authenticated users
  - Include Delete button for comment authors/post authors
  - Include Report button for authenticated users

### Validation & Features
- Comment body: 1-2000 characters (422 on validation failure)
- Reporting: Idempotent (multiple reports by same user count as one)
- Hiding: Comments with 3+ unique user reports are hidden from the page but remain in database
- Tests verify all functionality including edge cases

All checks pass: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test`, and `bunx guren gate`.
